title: IP over Avian Carriers with Quality of Service

hero.subtitle: Extending IP over Avian Carriers with Quality of Service mechanisms

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This memo amends RFC 1149 to allow for Quality of Service information to be included in datagrams transported on avian carriers. This is a follow-up April Fools' RFC that extends the original with modern networking concepts applied to pigeons.

Published on April 1, 1999, exactly nine years after RFC 1149, this document humorously applies Differentiated Services (DiffServ) and integrated services concepts to carrier pigeon networks.

sections.title: Improvements over RFC 1149
sections.content:
The original RFC 1149 specification did not address quality of service, congestion control, or multiple service classes. RFC 2549 adds these capabilities.

Service Classes
Traffic can be classified into different priority levels, with premium carriers (well-trained, experienced pigeons) handling high-priority traffic.
Congestion Control
When too many pigeons are launched simultaneously, mid-air collisions may occur. Proper spacing and traffic shaping are essential.
Error Detection
Physical inspection of the carrier upon arrival can detect transit damage. Waterproofing provides protection against weather-induced errors.

sections.title: Quality of Service
sections.content:
QoS for avian carriers is achieved through careful selection and training of carriers, route optimization, and weather monitoring.

Premium ServiceWell-rested, champion racing pigeons with GPS tracking
Standard ServiceRegular homing pigeons, best-effort delivery
Bulk ServiceAny available bird, including non-homing species (unreliable)

The Differentiated Services Code Point (DSCP) is encoded using colored leg bands. Red indicates Expedited Forwarding, blue indicates Assured Forwarding, and no band indicates Best Effort.

sections.title: The MstrStrpS Field
sections.content:
The Master Strap Security field provides authentication and integrity checking for avian carrier datagrams.

MstrStrpS Security Levels
Level 0: No security (no strap)
Level 1: Simple strap (tamper-evident tape)
Level 2: Sealed capsule (weather-resistant)
Level 3: GPS-tracked capsule with biometric lock

Security considerations note that avian carriers are vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks by hawks, cats, and other predators. End-to-end encryption is strongly recommended for all sensitive datagrams.

sections.title: Updated Frame Format
sections.content:
The frame format extends RFC 1149 with additional fields for QoS marking, security classification, and carrier health indicators.

Extended Avian Carrier Frame
+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
|  QoS Class  |  Security Lvl  |
+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
|        Carrier ID             |
+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
|    IP Datagram (on scroll)    |
|          (variable)           |
+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
|       Checksum (visual)       |
+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
Feature
RFC 1149
RFC 2549
QoS Support
None
3 service classes
Security
None
4 security levels
Tracking
None
GPS optional
